newsitem.title: IRAQ: Turkish firms exhibit products in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkish firms exhibit products in Iraq.

text.p: Forty-two Turkish companies displayed their products on Tuesday in Baghdad to sell food and medicine to Iraq under its oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations last year.
The trade fair, opened by Iraqi Finance Minister Hikmat Mezban Ibrahim, included food, farm machinery and medical equipment.
Ibrahim did not say whether Iraq would buy anything from the exhibiting firms. But he described trade ties between the two countries as "growing and there are new horizons of wider cooperation".

The oil-for-food deal allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to raise money to buy food and medicine for Iraqis, suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed on Baghdad for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
